source.title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models
source.authors: Giovana Kerche Bonás; T. Almeida; Marcelo Henrique da Silva Reis; Rodrigo Nogueira; Marcos M. Raimundo

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices and tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses prior refusal-direction work but tests its own directions for unsafe tool-call behavior. It does not test the refusal direction or refusal behavior named in the claim; tool-call violations are explicitly treated as distinct from textual refusal.
record.gate_note: The study estimates behavior-weighted directions from BF16 activations and unsafe-tool-call labels, then adds or subtracts them at one selected layer. It does not estimate the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or ablate it. Its main outcome is harmful tool-call proposals (and, in SODA, executed harmful actions), not refusal of harmful user requests or refusal of harmless requests. Zero-strength Qwen suppression rows are baseline aliases, not suppression tests. Several control, probe, label-yield, and geometry results are described in the text but are not results on the claimed refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The study estimates its own behavior-weighted directions (activations weighted by unsafe-tool-call fractions), adds or subtracts them at one layer, and measures unsafe tool-call proposals and executed unsafe trajectories. Its violation definition counts a harmful call as a violation even when prose refuses. It does not estimate a harmful-minus-harmless direction, does not ablate one, and reports no refusal rate. The paper cites Arditi et al. only as background. Its results bear on a related construct (unsafe tool action), not on any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that a direction estimated once in BF16 transfers across precision (NF4 labels act like native ones, differing by ≤1.8 pp), across languages (including held-out Arabic) and across scale up to 70B. They add that transfer is uneven, receiver-native directions remain competitive, and effect sizes depend on the judge.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a centered, behavior-weighted BF16 activation association with unsafe tool-call fractions, not the claimed harmful-minus-harmless instruction difference in mean activations. It adds or subtracts a direction at one selected layer during input processing and generation; it does not project a refusal direction out of every layer and position or add it to induce harmless-request refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary across models, languages, intervention signs and estimators. The paper reports uneven cross-language transfer and evaluator dependence; for Llama-3.1-70B suppression, the reported effect ranges from −12.38 to −38.62 percentage points across judges. Qwen has no selected nonzero suppression strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Behavior-weighted directions at one layer raise or lower unsafe tool-call proposals. Effects range from +76.5 pp (Qwen3.5-9B) to about ±6 pp (Ministral-3-8B), with BFCL changes of −2.84 to +1.20 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-layer activation directions estimated from unsafe-tool-call labels causally modulate harmful tool-call proposals in tool-calling LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Tool-action directions transfer across scales via benign-anchor maps and to held-out Arabic, but unevenly. Ministral shows no Arabic effect, and a permuted-label control exceeds transport in Llama-70B induction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsafe-tool-action directions transfer across languages and model scales, with model-dependent magnitude and limited direction specificity.

fits_no_version.finding: The same interventions change executed unsafe trajectories in SODA for some models and signs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tool-action steering effects carry over to executed agent trajectories in simulated environments for some models.

record.problems: The paper notes small scenario partitions and incomplete independence between scenarios; Qwen layer validation has very few positive responses. Unsafe-action labels are model-judged without human validation, judge disagreement is substantial in the Llama-3.1-70B audit, and intervals condition on selected directions and strengths and omit judge error and selection uncertainty. Arabic has only 11 test scenarios, and benign capability controls are English-only. Proposed LUMEN calls are not executed; SODA uses simulated environments. Scale transfer requires receiver access and validation outcomes for tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the zero-strength Qwen suppression aliases, because the paper states they reuse baseline responses and do not test suppression. Detailed per-language transfer matrix cells, individual random-direction controls, probe measures, construction label counts, and training-only LoRA comparisons are omitted; they are not refusal-direction outcomes, and the main reported transfer and behavior results are represented above.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless direction, ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts, capability preservation under that direction
Jailbreaks acting through the direction; adversarial training
Multi-direction or cone structure of refusal
Harmfulness encoding separate from the refusal decision
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, scales or base/instruct. Transfer is shown only for tool-action directions.
Training dependence of the refusal direction
Reasoning models; Qwen models are run with thinking disabled

record.verdict_notes: The title expands PRISM as 'Probing Refusal Internals' and the related work cites Arditi et al. Even so, the endpoint is explicitly tool-action violation, distinct from textual refusal. The record's T6/discusses classification is kept; an argument could be made for T4, but the study does not use the refusal direction as a tool. The Llama-70B judge dependence (−12.38 to −38.62 pp) and the random-direction and permuted-label controls are relevant only to the fits_no_version claims.

versions.untested_parts: No test of the claimed refusal direction, all-layer/all-position ablation or addition, refusal of harmful requests, refusal of harmless requests, or general ability preservation under that direction.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the claimed refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
The paper tests transfer of its own unsafe-tool-action directions, not transfer of the claimed refusal direction or refusal behavior.
No test of how refusal training timing or method determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
No reasoning-model test of the claimed refusal-direction mechanism.
